solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Medicinal plant creates calm that is wafting round Medical Officer

indicators.note: round says the reshuffled letters go around the next abbreviation
wafting means drifting about, so the letters of calm plus the abbreviation are blown into a new order

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A soothing herb is said to bring calm, its scent drifting around the doctor on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creates' is only a link. The scrambled letters give CAMILE, and the doctor's abbreviation sits after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamomile is a herb whose flowers are used to make a soothing medicinal tea.

clue.text: Friends, for instance. Divine one's what its maker has confused in 12

definitions.meaning: Friends is a famous TV sitcom, an example of the genre

definitions.text: Divine one's what its maker has confused in 12
definitions.meaning: Dante wrote the Divine one; his name appears jumbled within the letters of the answer at 12 across

explanation.walkthrough: DANTE's letters appear scrambled inside DILETTANTE, the answer to 12.
explanation.definitionFit: Friends is a sitcom, a humorous genre, and Dante's poem is called the Divine Comedy.

clue.text: Digital game learner supports as having virtue

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports sits beneath, so the learner goes at the bottom

parts.note: mora is a finger-counting guessing game, digital as played with the fingers
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A finger game with a novice holding things up, described as virtuous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' means using the digits, not electronic.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral as an adjective describes someone virtuous, with good principles.

clue.text: Male nurse must put out solvents for pharmacist

indicators.note: put out suggests the letters of nurse must being disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A man working as a nurse needs to throw away a chemist's liquids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges the nine letters into ENSTRUUMS; this plural of an old pharmacy term is rare.
explanation.definitionFit: A menstruum is an old pharmaceutical term for a solvent used to extract drugs.

clue.text: Spring is part of the year

indicators.note: part of shows the letters are found inside the words the year

explanation.surface: Springtime is one season of the twelve months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season but means a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye can mean the source of a spring of water, where it rises from the ground.

clue.text: Worries son will be seen as a soft touch

parts.note: worries as a noun are cares or anxieties
S is the usual abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: Anxieties about a boy turn out to be mere gentleness, a tender gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: A caress is a gentle stroke, literally a light, soft touch of the hand.

clue.text: Dutch 4-1 up for it? More than up for it

indicators.note: up in a down clue tells the solver to read the letters from the bottom upwards

parts.note: 4 in Roman numerals is IV and 1 is A, as in a single one

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Dutch bettor will take odds of four to one; they are keener still.
explanation.walkthrough: '4-1' looks like betting odds. Read up, D IV A gives the opera singer DIVA backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or keen, so stronger than merely willing.

clue.text: Empire he'd built? It's short-lived

indicators.note: built suggests the letters of empire he'd being constructed in a new order

explanation.surface: A comment that an empire someone constructed did not last long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built' rearranges EMPIRE HED.
explanation.definitionFit: An ephemerid is a mayfly, an insect whose adult life lasts only a day or so.

clue.text: In second contest between states Kentucky and South Dakota turned up

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky
a war is a contest between nations

indicators.note: turned tells the solver to flip the two letters for this state around

parts.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for South Dakota

explanation.surface: A rematch between two American states, Kentucky and South Dakota, ends in an upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'states' looks like American states but means nations; 'turned' flips SD to DS.
explanation.definitionFit: Skywards means towards the sky, that is, in an upward direction.

clue.text: Take in heavenly body, one that's not very bright

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for take inside the word for the heavenly body

parts.note: the moon is the heavenly body nearest Earth
R abbreviates recipe, Latin for take, as written on old prescriptions

explanation.surface: An instruction to absorb a celestial object, which is then dismissed as rather dim.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the moon shining, while 'not very bright' means unintelligent. R for 'take' is the prescription symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A moron is a stupid person, someone who is not very bright in the intellectual sense.

clue.text: How he fills breaks in Seychelles?

definitions.text: How he fills breaks in Seychelles?

indicators.note: breaks in suggests the letters are broken apart and reassembled

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle registration code for the Seychelles

explanation.surface: A question about how a man stuffs himself on holiday in the Indian Ocean islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks in' rearranges HE FILLS with SY. The whole clue also reads as a description: he fills himself, looking after number one.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting selfishly means acting only for one's own benefit, as someone filling himself up while on a break.

clue.text: Trying to please I see pink all over

indicators.note: over suggests the letters are knocked over and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone eager to please spots pink everywhere, perhaps blushing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' rearranges I SEE PINK ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaniels are proverbially fawning and eager, so a fawning manner is like that of the dog.

clue.text: W.I. all met, not fussing about Miss March, perhaps, my wife

indicators.note: fussing about suggests the letters moving restlessly into a new order

explanation.surface: Women's Institute members all gathered calmly to discuss a Miss March.
explanation.walkthrough: W.I. is the Women's Institute, a British countryside women's club. Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy March are the heroines of Alcott's Little Women; the phrase is also an old-fashioned term for one's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Each March sister in Alcott's novel is one of its title characters, and the phrase is old-fashioned slang for a spouse.

clue.text: One who dabbles in literature and is remarkably talented with it

indicators.note: remarkably hints at something unusual, so the letters of talented and it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A literary amateur who, surprisingly, turns out to be gifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkably' rearranges TALENTED + IT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante is an amateur who takes up the arts superficially rather than seriously.

clue.text: Egyptian girl who dances round tree

indicators.note: round signals the letters of the dancing girl's name being turned about into a new order

parts.note: an alma (or almah) is an Egyptian dancing girl

explanation.surface: An Egyptian dancer circles a tree, like a maypole dance.
explanation.walkthrough: ALMA is a crossword word for an Egyptian dancing girl; 'round' rearranges it, swapping L and M.
explanation.definitionFit: The amla is an Indian tree, source of the Indian gooseberry fruit.

clue.text: With Scots dirk may be concealed weapon

indicators.note: may be signals the letters could be arranged into something else

explanation.surface: A Scottish dagger may serve as a hidden blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges W + SCOTS DIRK.
explanation.definitionFit: A swordstick is a walking cane containing a blade, a weapon kept out of sight.

clue.text: Deformity attributed to ring could be a clue for Lawrie

definitions.text: Deformity attributed to ring could be a clue for Lawrie

parts.words: Deformity attributed to ring could be a clue for Lawrie
parts.note: a boxer's swollen, misshapen lug comes from bouts in the ring; Lawrie is a name a setter might clue with it

explanation.surface: A boxing injury is suggested as a crossword hint for someone named Lawrie.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring is a boxing ring, where repeated blows thicken the outer ear.
explanation.definitionFit: This swollen, lumpy deformity of the outer organ of hearing is typical of boxers and rugby players.

clue.text: Place card setting. Does it mean trouble ahead for babies?

indicators.note: setting suggests the letters of place card being set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Laying out name cards at a table, with a question about trouble looming for infants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' rearranges PLACE CARD. 'trouble ahead' means a problem on the head, not in the future.
explanation.definitionFit: Cradle cap is a scaly scalp condition common in infants, literally a problem on the head.

clue.text: See 15
Former partner in mine is left in charge. That's clear

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: in places the abbreviations for left and in charge inside the word for a mine

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Someone's former partner, now running a mine, makes things plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like the possessive but is a coal pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Explicit means stated plainly and fully, leaving nothing unclear.

clue.text: I didn't expect to see you as old — still warm. Let it all go …

definitions.text: I didn't expect to see you

indicators.note: letting it all go suggests releasing the preceding letters to fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A surprised greeting to someone looking aged, then a plea to relax and give up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let it all go' rearranges AS OLD STILL WARM, fourteen letters, into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the stock exclamation of surprise on bumping into an acquaintance somewhere unexpected.

clue.text: See 17
Ground for grazing one mowed irregularly

indicators.note: irregularly suggests the letters of a and mowed fall out of order

parts.note: A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A field for livestock that someone has cut unevenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregularly' rearranges A + MOWED.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow is a grassy field, often used as pasture for animals.

clue.text: … hang! Lots of love, Lambert

parts.note: LOL is the texting abbreviation for lots of love
L is the symbol for the lambert, a unit of luminance

explanation.surface: A letter signed off with affection by someone called Lambert, after an exasperated exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: Lambert looks like a signature but is the unit of brightness, symbol L.
explanation.definitionFit: To loll is to droop or dangle loosely, as a tongue lolls out of a dog's mouth.

clue.text: D is letter pointing to door

parts.note: a missive is a letter or written message

explanation.surface: A sign explaining that the letter D marks the way to an exit.
explanation.walkthrough: D and IS are taken as written; 'pointing to door' means showing someone out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being curtly sent away, shown the exit, is a contemptuous rejection, so the manner is curt and rejecting.

clue.text: Independent state with quiet people

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A sovereign country and its peaceful inhabitants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Independent state' looks like a nation, but it is I plus a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: The inhabitants of Ireland are collectively called by this name, a nationality.

clue.text: Vestment he lost at Prestonpans

definitions.meaning: a long cloak-like garment worn by clergy
Sir John ... commanded the government army defeated at Prestonpans in 1745

explanation.walkthrough: Prestonpans, near Edinburgh, was a Jacobite victory over the British government army in 1745.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a priest's long ceremonial cloak and the surname of the defeated general.

clue.text: Vast empty city with no place to settle

indicators.note: empty means the inside of the word city is removed, leaving only its ends
to settle suggests the letters of no place shifting until they settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A huge abandoned city with nowhere for newcomers to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves CY from city; 'to settle' rearranges NO PLACE into CLOPEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclopean describes massive structures, as if built by the giant Cyclops, hence huge.

clue.text: Tune to be broadcast

definitions.meaning: to put out on radio or television

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a melody, and as a verb to transmit a programme on radio or television.

clue.text: Epic's title I said regularly

definitions.note: Epic's reads as 'Epic is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: regularly means taking every second letter of title I said

explanation.surface: A remark about the name of a long poem, which the speaker claims to have spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of TITLE I SAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's poem about the siege of Troy is the archetypal ancient Greek epic.

clue.text: Hat — a good sort

definitions.meaning: old slang for a decent, excellent person

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a tall formal hat and, informally, a thoroughly good fellow.

clue.text: Was rich king conveyed by it?

definitions.text: Was rich king conveyed by it?

indicators.note: conveyed suggests the letters being carried along and shifted into a new order

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Asks whether a wealthy monarch was carried about in some vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conveyed' rearranges WAS RICH + K; the whole clue also describes the hand-pulled cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A rickshaw is a light two-wheeled carriage pulled by a person, conveying passengers.
